findings.message: 15 mm2 of artwork across 2 shapes is claimed by a shape the design sews, but no thread lands on it (largest bare patch 4 mm2). A limb or corner is missing from the stitch-out even though the shape itself looks correct. Check the named shapes in review before sewing.

Isacord Polyester 40 0020 (Black) is clearly a different color than 2 of the 3 shapes it sews (worst: S371d740b, 7.27 mm² — 0.49% of the design). Pick a closer thread or a different brand before sewing.

9 of 15 satin shapes sew below readable size at this scale — columns under 1 mm or details under 4 mm. Enlarging helps but does not fully clear it: the smallest shapes regenerate at any size. Remove or simplify the smallest lettering.

2 satin shapes sew the gaps between their own strokes closed at 63 mm: Sc1b3904f (29.8 x 11.3 mm) has 50% of the space between its strokes narrower than 1.2 mm, the pull compensation (0.4 mm a side) plus a 0.4 mm thread on Structured cap. Connected lettering and marks with spokes do this; the lever is the size. Its tightest tenth of gap clears that at about 151 mm of design width.

4.5 trims per 1,000 stitches — professional files run 0.1 to 4.1. Each cut is 2-3 seconds of machine time. 31 of 33 are moves between shapes, so merging or removing the smallest is the cheapest thing to try; the other 2 are inside a shape and it will not touch them.

Reading the stitched design back, 4 of the 6 text clusters is damaged on the thread: the artwork reads ‘1895’ where the thread reads ‘HERE’ (0% of the letters match). Make the lettering bigger or simpler before sewing.

130 mm2 of this design stacks more than 6.66667 layers of thread on one patch of fabric (peak 10.6), counting underlay, fill and outlines together. That much thread puckers the garment and breaks needles. The worst of 2 is 85 mm2 near (5, 1) mm. Check that the layers there are meant to overlap.

That is usually the page behind the logo rather than part of it. Sewn, it fills the garment with thread the color of the cloth and leaves the logo as bare fabric. Delete that shape in review, or confirm the background really is meant to sew.
